## Natural history notes

A large marsh bird characterized by a long slightly downcurved bill, brown body streaked with white, long legs, and loud wailing calls often heard around wetlands. In Florida, the Limpkin is found in freshwater marshes, swamps, ponds, lakes, canals, sloughs, and wet prairies, especially where apple snails are abundant. It feeds mainly on apple snails by using its specialized bill to extract them from their shells, but it also eats mussels, insects, crustaceans, and other small aquatic animals, nesting in dense marsh vegetation or low shrubs near water.
